message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported revenue of $1.85 billion for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, up 36.54% from a year earlier, with net income of $397 million, up 107.85%, a gross margin of 65.87% and a net margin of 21.51% [D1]. Communications Solutions Group revenue was $1,345 million, up 43.09%, and Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue was $501 million, up 21.6% [D1]. Guidance for the fourth quarter is revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion, with the mid-point representing growth of about 37%, and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 on a diluted share count of approximately 172 million [D1].

What the market is arguing about is whether the demand behind the record quarter is durable and whether supply rather than demand now governs how much of that demand becomes revenue, with analysts pressing management on the sustainability of its order levels and on whether supply constraints are capping guidance [D3]. Management said supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue and that the supply situation is likely to be nonlinear [D3]. Management also cautioned that the one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 artificially pulled up profitability and will not repeat, which sets a high comparison bar for future periods [D3]. Against that, management said demand is far exceeding its ability to supply and that the pipeline continues to grow strongly [D3].

The plan is therefore to stay with the uptrend while the fourth quarter delivers revenue inside the guided range of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and earnings per share inside the guided range of 3.34 to 3.40 [D1]. The first evidence that the comparison bar is biting would be a gross margin below the latest quarter's 65.87% or a net margin below 21.51% [D1]. The first evidence that conversion rather than demand is the binding constraint would be revenue at or below the bottom of the guided range [D1].
